claim: Foraminiferal shells are generated by chambers added in logarithmic-spiral succession with (near-)constant growth ratios, and the genera form a continuous geometric series transformable into one another.

dataset.name: Data from: Heterochronic origin of spherical fusulinid foraminifera in the Late Paleozoic
dataset.match: fusulinid foraminifera half-whorl outlines — same taxon class and variable as Thompson's von Moller Fusulina exemplar (p. 593); whorl-level, not septal-chamber-level

T1_geometric_succession.rule: median Pearson r(log D, k) >= 0.98 and geometric beats arithmetic (BIC) in >= 80 % of specimens

T2_near_constant_ratio.rule: median CV of successive half-whorl ratios <= 0.15 ('small secondary fluctuation', p. 595)

T3_fusulina_ratio_1_225.rule: Triticites (triticitid fusulinid, cf. von Moller's Fusulina) mean half-whorl ratio within 0.05 of 1.225

T4_continuous_series.rule: no interior (5-95 %) gap in the pooled per-specimen ratio distribution larger than 6x the median gap, and every pair of genera adjacent in mean ratio has overlapping ranges (genera grade into one another)
